てびちのてーすけ.name: Tebichi no Tesuke
てびちのてーすけ.desc: A pig's feet (tebichi) specialty shop recognizable by its laid-back pig sign. Its signature is the “Tesuke Special,” topped with pig's feet, braised pork belly, soft-bone pork ribs, yushi-dofu, and sea lettuce — everything. A light tebichi soba to enjoy with vinegar and shikuwasa pepper. They also sell seasoned frozen pig's feet and horse sashimi.
t: * This article was created with AI (Chat GPT 5 Thinking) and partly supplemented by me 😁
I ate here in December 2024 😆 This time I went to “Tebichi no Tesuke” in Sashiki Shinkai, Nanjo City.
Tebichi no Tesuke
Tebichi no Tesuke

In a corner of a well-worn building, a handwritten “Open” sign and a laid-back pig sign greet you boldly. As in the photo, “Tebichi specialty shop” is written in big letters, and artificial turf is laid in front of the shop, giving it a nice hideaway feel 🐷
Inside the shop
As for condiments, there is no kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori) — instead there is vinegar and shikuwasa pepper.
There is also a panel on how to eat tebichi
Inside, the counter and tables are compactly arranged, with figurines casually displayed, giving it a relaxed, homey feel.
Menu
Menu
Menu
Tesuke Special　¥1,300

From the menu I ordered the “Tesuke Special” without hesitation. With the dignity of an “everything on top” bowl, pig's feet (tebichi), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), yushi-dofu, and sea lettuce (āsa) — the tastiest parts of Okinawa — are all packed into one bowl. The blended broth has a somewhat strong bonito stock and a noticeable saltiness.
Tesuke Special　¥1,300
The noodles are medium-thin fresh noodles, slightly wavy. They're chewy 🍜

The star, the pig's feet, is wobbly-soft. The skin melts, and sweetness spreads each time the layers of collagen unravel. The seasoning is quite restrained, and as the notice on the table says “we recommend adding vinegar,” a single drizzle brings out a sharp crispness all at once. The braised pork belly leans light. It has a little sinewy texture. The soft-bone pork ribs are soft right through to the bone.

The yushi-dofu topping is soft and gentle, and its sweetness swells further once it absorbs the broth. The green of the sea lettuce brings the scent of the sea, adding Okinawan flavor to the scene in the bowl, which is nice too. The condiments of shirogaki-negi (shredded green onion) and julienned ginger sharpen the outline, and it felt designed to run from start to finish as a “light tebichi soba.” There's no kōrēgūsu on the table; instead there is shikuwasa pepper, which pairs wonderfully. The citrus freshness lifts the broth's saltiness and the bonito aroma, and neatly pulls together the aftertaste. Toward the end, I dissolved a little chili paste, and the slow-building heat of the spice made my forehead sweat. Yet the outline of the broth doesn't collapse, and it let me drink it down happily to the end. By the time I finished eating, I was warmed from the core of my body 🔥

On the wall there is also a poster titled “How to eat tebichi deliciously,” and it's interesting that it carefully guides you through using vinegar, Tabasco, and even turning it into a broth-over-rice dish.
I'd like to try the bone soup soba too 😄

By the register there's also a notice for the “bone soup soba.” I thought I'd like to go for that next time. In the merchandise corner, in addition to seasoned frozen pig's feet, they even sell horse sashimi. It's an enticing lineup that makes you want to take it home as a snack for drinking at home, and my purse strings almost loosened. I felt that the reason for its popularity lies not only in the bowl but also in how it creates this kind of “room for enjoyment” 😊

Rating (9/15): All in all, it was a reassuring bowl for which the words “just plain tasty” fit perfectly, without any gimmicks. It pleasantly betrays the image that tebichi means rich and heavy, with a lightness that leaves no heaviness after the meal, which I like ✌️
When you come to Nanjo City, why not give it a try once?

そば処 じゅりあん.name: Soba-dokoro Jurian
そば処 じゅりあん.desc: A shop with an additive-free (no chemical seasoning) broth of bonito, kelp, and Agu pork bone. The soft-bone pork ribs soba (regular) is a reasonable ¥640, and there is a ¥100 discount service when you show your Itomaru parking lot ticket.
t: I ate here in November 2023. This shop is a participating shop in the “13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29),” and I went as the 21st of 34 shops 😊
Soba-dokoro Jurian

This shop has no parking lot, but a few dozen meters away on foot there is a large paid parking lot at “Itoman Market Itomaru,” and according to the stamp rally booklet, “show your parking ticket for a one-hour fee cashback,” so the parking problem seems fine 😁
The paid parking lot of “Itoman Market Itomaru”
The paid parking lot of “Itoman Market Itomaru”
Inside the shop (it's fairly large)
Inside the shop (it's fairly large)
For my order I chose the “soft-bone pork ribs soba (regular) with soft-boiled egg topping” introduced in the stamp rally booklet.
Menu (with toppings)
Menu (without toppings)

The “soft-bone pork ribs soba (regular) with soft-boiled egg topping” I ordered is ¥640, but when I showed my parking ticket they said “we'll take ¥100 off,” making it ¥540 😊 You don't see this price range much at other shops; I think it's reasonable.
“Soft-bone pork ribs soba (regular) with soft-boiled egg topping” ¥640 → ¥540 (with parking cashback)
First, a sip of the broth. This shop's broth is made with bonito, kelp, and Agu pork bone with no chemical seasoning, so they are particular about ingredients. The flavor is gentle too.
“Soft-bone pork ribs soba (regular) with soft-boiled egg topping” ¥640 → ¥540 (with parking cashback)

Next, the noodles 🤗 They are medium-thick straight noodles and on the soft side. The soft-bone pork ribs also seem to be seasoned with preservative-free soy sauce; there was a little sinewy texture, but they were tender and gently flavored.
After finishing, when leaving the paid parking lot, I inserted my parking ticket to put in the cashback ¥100, and to my surprise the display said “¥0” (;^ω^)
I think it's because I finished eating in a short 10 to 20 minutes and took my car out. In the end, the soba came to a quite reasonable ¥540, lol

Rating (9/15): It's just plain tasty 😊 Moreover, if you leave the parking lot early, the parking fee is free and you also get the ¥100 cashback with the parking ticket at the shop, so effectively you can have Okinawa soba at a reasonable price 😁

沖縄そば 金太郎.name: Okinawa Soba Kintaro
沖縄そば 金太郎.desc: A hugely popular shop famous for “Minami Jiro,” the Okinawa soba version of Ramen Jiro. A soy-sauce-based ramen using fresh Okinawa soba noodles, authentic Jiro style where you're asked about the amount of vegetables and garlic. Hearty portions, recommended for those who want to eat their fill.
t: I went to eat here in February 2024 😄 I learned about this shop from a newspaper, and I was curious because it apparently has an Okinawa soba version of “Ramen Jiro,” which I had experienced for the first time in Tokyo in October 2023, so I came to eat 😄
Okinawa Soba Kintaro
Incidentally, the image below is my X post from when I first ate “Ramen Jiro” in Tokyo (^0^;)

I went without doing detailed research, and since the customer in front of me ordered “small,” I thought “small” literally means less and ordered “small,” but I was shocked when it arrived, lol I ate and ate but the amount never went down, it got painful, and I gave up with half left (^0^;)
Tweet from my first Ramen Jiro experience 😆 I gave up with half left (^0^;)

How about this “Okinawa Soba Kintaro”? I came several dozen minutes before opening, and right before it opened there were lots of customers. The parking lot filled up immediately too. I thought it's definitely a popular shop.
Menu posted at the shop entrance (the item called “Minami Jiro” seems to be the Jiro-style Okinawa soba 😆)
Menu posted at the shop entrance (besides the soba menu there are rice bowl dishes too 😄)
Inside the shop there is a ticket machine, and I ordered the “Minami Jiro.” The sizes are large and medium, but just in case I ordered “medium” (^0^;)
This ticket machine supports cashless payment, and I was able to pay with PayPay. Cashless is great 👍
When I ordered “Minami Jiro, medium,” the staff asked “How would you like the amount of vegetables and garlic?” so I ordered “extra, please.”
Will I be okay? Will I repeat the mistake of Tokyo's Ramen Jiro? My heart is pounding (^0^;)
Inside the shop (it's quite spacious)
Minami Jiro (medium)　¥900
Here it comes. Like the original “Ramen Jiro,” you can't see the noodles (^0^;)
First I taste the broth. As the menu says “This is ramen using fresh Okinawa soba noodles,” the broth is soy-sauce-based and it's already ramen (^0^;)
But it's just plain tasty. Next I want to taste the noodles, but I can't see them and don't seem able to reach them, so I eat the vegetables, chashu, and garlic bit by bit (^0^;)
The broth has a strong flavor and contains garlic, so at any rate it has punch.
Minami Jiro (medium)　¥900

I reached the noodles and tasted them. Chewy fresh noodles, just plain tasty. I asked for extra vegetables and garlic with the medium size; naturally the amount is smaller than a small at the original “Ramen Jiro,” but it's still full of volume, and I think it is more than the large size at other shops. I managed to finish it all 😄

Rating (9/15): It was ramen, practically 😄 The flavor is strong and punchy, and the portion is large too, so I recommend it to those who want to eat their fill. Incidentally, the amount of garlic is also extreme, so your mouth will smell of garlic all day, lol

みらい食堂.name: Mirai Shokudo
みらい食堂.desc: A diner that used to be inside Michi-no-Eki Ginoza (* now closed). Its Okinawa soba featured the signature “jagamen,” noodles kneaded with potatoes from Ginoza Village, and the Ginoza soba topped with pig's feet, braised pork belly, pork spare ribs, and egg omelet was hearty. I'm keeping this article as a record.
t: I ate here in January 2021.
Note: Unfortunately this shop is now closed. I'm writing it down as a record.
Mirai Shokudo (inside the Ginoza Village roadside station) “In the photo it says ‘Taiyotei,’ but I'm not sure why ^^;”
Menu (at Mirai Shokudo, the noodles are “jagamen,” made with potatoes from Ginoza Village)
Ginoza soba, large　¥750

I ordered the “Ginoza soba, large.” The noodles are medium-thin, made from potatoes. The broth is bonito stock and delicious 😋 There seemed to be no difference from ordinary noodles ^^; The toppings were hearty too, with pig's feet (tebichi), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), pork spare ribs (soki), and egg omelet.

Rating (9/15): It was just plain tasty, but it's a pity it has closed. Ginoza Village promotes itself as a potato village, and the road lighting fixtures in the area are designed as “potatoes,” so please take a look when you pass nearby 😁 It seems to be a shop called “Shokudo Manjiro?” now, so maybe they have Okinawa soba using “jagamen.”

みーなみ.name: Mīnami
みーなみ.desc: A local diner that pushes its goat (yagi) dishes (there is even a goat sashimi vending machine!). The classic Okinawa soba comes with free fuchiba on a separate plate, so you can change the flavor partway and enjoy it to the end. Its unpretentious atmosphere with table and tatami seating is charming.
t: For this Okinawa soba outing, I went to “Mīnami” in Minami-Uehara, Nakagusuku Village 🌞 I ate here in March 2025 😄
Mīnami
Outdoor vending machine (it's all goat (^0^;))

The exterior has a bright sign like a blue sky, giving it a somewhat laid-back feel. At first glance it's simple and approachable, but when you look at the vending machine and banners beside the entrance, the presence of goat dishes such as goat soup and goat sashimi is quite strong, and you immediately think “oh, this shop pushes goat,” which makes a strong impression 🐐
Inside the shop
Inside the shop

Inside, the wood-grain walls give a calm atmosphere, with table seats and tatami seating, and it definitely has an old-fashioned diner feel 😊 I personally like this unpretentious feel quite a bit. It didn't feel designed for tourists, but like a place that is an extension of everyday life where local people just come to eat.
Menu
Looking at the menu boards, goat soba, goat soup set meal, soki soba, and more were lined up, showing this shop's character. Among them I chose the “Okinawa soba (braised pork belly), large” 👀
Okinawa soba (braised pork belly), large　¥800

The Okinawa soba that arrived was quite classic just from looking at it. With a slightly clear broth, medium-thin straight noodles, braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), fish cake (kamaboko), and green onions, it has a comforting quality that makes you want to say “this is diner Okinawa soba” 🍥 Also, free fuchiba comes on a separate plate, which was a nice touch 🌿 A service like this is quietly appreciated. At first you eat it as is, and then you can change the flavor partway, so it's easy to eat without getting bored until the end.

First the broth. My impression after one sip was that it's probably a blended broth, but neither pork bone nor bonito pushed to the front. There was also a faint gentle sweetness, making it easy to drink ☺️ But for better or worse the individuality was faint, without an obvious punch like “the bonito is strong!” or “the pork-bone richness is strong!” It's not that the balance is off at all, but honestly, as for whether it's a broth that leaves a strong impression, it doesn't quite reach that.
Okinawa soba (braised pork belly), large　¥800

The noodles were medium-thin straight noodles, finished on the soft side. The noodles themselves didn't have a strong presence, and neither in texture nor aroma did they make me think “these noodles are great.” Not bad, but my impression is that it's an overall mild bowl.

The braised pork belly was moderately well-seasoned, neither too strong nor too weak, and the balance there was not bad 🥢 It wasn't sweet-and-salty to the point of pushing itself forward, so it didn't spoil the broth's character. However, when I ate it, the sinewy texture was rather strong, and it wasn't the type that falls apart. It has a chew, but if it had a bit more fat tenderness and melt-in-the-mouth quality, the satisfaction would go up another notch. Including the fish cake and green onions, the toppings overall are quite basic, giving the impression of an old-fashioned bowl without gimmicks.

And when I added the fuchiba partway through, it made quite a nice accent 🌿✨ To a broth that was a little mild as is, the fuchiba's characteristic aroma and faint bitterness were added, and the flavor tightened up. Rather than putting it all in from the start, adding it a bit at a time as I watched was more enjoyable. Thanks to this free topping, I could eat without it getting too monotonous until the end. Honestly, where it would have ended with “it's ordinary” with the plain state alone, the fuchiba lifted it a little 😌

Rating (9/15): My overall impression settles at “this is really just ordinary Okinawa soba.” Of course that's not only in a bad sense; it means it has no odd quirks and is a standard bowl you can eat with confidence at a diner 🍜 But if you ask whether I'd go all the way from afar for this Okinawa soba, I didn't feel it was decisive enough. Precisely because it's a shop with prominent goat dishes, I thought it would be interesting if the standard Okinawa soba had a bit more character too. Still, as a bowl you can eat casually in a calm interior while changing the flavor with the free fuchiba, it wasn't bad 🙂 It was the kind of Okinawa soba shop you'd drop into on a whim if you were nearby.
